actions.actionEn: Define a clear Lean strategic vision with precise operational objectives and communicate it at every level of the organisation.
actions.actionFr: Définir une vision stratégique Lean claire avec des objectifs opérationnels précis et les communiquer à tous les niveaux de l'organisation.
steps: Run a leadership workshop to define a 3-5 year Lean 'True North' (quality, lead time, cost, safety, people) tied to business strategy
Translate the vision into 3-5 annual breakthrough objectives with numeric targets (Hoshin Kanri / X-matrix)
Cascade objectives to plant/department level through catchball so each area owns 1-3 measurable Lean goals
Communicate the vision at every level (town hall, shop-floor boards, onboarding) and check understanding on gemba walks
actions.durationBasis: practice; Hoshin Kanri runs as an annual cycle and the first vision/objective set is usually drafted in one planning quarter (Reich, Planet Lean; IndustryWeek on Toyota strategy deployment)
actions.proof: Signed Lean vision/True North document and Hoshin (X-matrix) with numeric annual objectives, cascaded department objectives, and a sample of employees able to state the Lean objectives of their area.
kpis: Objective deployment rate = departments with documented Lean objectives / total departments x 100 (%)
Vision awareness = employees correctly stating area Lean goals / employees sampled x 100 (%)
actions.example: Toyota North America (late 1990s-early 2000s) set a long-term vision for 2010 and created a structured annual hoshin planning process, with plant and HR leaders owning cross-company initiatives; over the period sales and production capacity tripled and plants grew from about 3 to 10-12 (as reported by Mark Reich, LEI).
actions.sectorNotes: Manufacturing/automotive firms often inherit the vision from a parent production system (Moroccan automotive OpEx is strongly driven by international parent companies); services and SMEs need to write their own, simpler vision in non-manufacturing language.
actions.pitfalls: Vision framed only as a toolkit or cost-cutting programme (44% of Moroccan automotive respondents saw OpEx as a set of tools vs 16% as a management approach); Hoshin introduced before the organisation has basic problem-solving and daily management maturity.

actions.actionEn: Allocate a dedicated budget to support Lean improvement projects and make it a key part of the annual financial plan.
actions.actionFr: Allouer un budget spécifique pour soutenir les projets d'amélioration Lean et en faire un élément clé du plan financier annuel.
steps: Create a Lean budget line in the annual financial plan (training, kaizen event time, small equipment, external coaching)
Staff a Kaizen Promotion Office with full-time internal people (rule of thumb 1-2% of hourly workforce) without adding headcount
Protect staff time for kaizen events as a budgeted cost, not overtime
Track realised savings against the Lean budget each quarter and reinvest part of savings into the programme
actions.durationBasis: practice; aligned with the next budget cycle; KPO staffing guidance from Art Byrne (LEI)
actions.proof: Approved annual budget with a dedicated Lean line, named KPO/Lean staff (FTE count), and a quarterly savings-vs-spend report.
kpis: Lean ROI = verified annual Lean savings / annual Lean spend (ratio)
Lean FTE ratio = full-time Lean/KPO staff / total headcount x 100 (%)
Budget execution = Lean spend actual / Lean budget x 100 (%)
actions.example: Royal Bolton Hospital NHS Trust (from late 2005) reports that the cash outlay on its Bolton Improving Care System was relatively small, though staff time input was considerable; almost GBP 300,000 of laundry savings and additional commercial income more than funded the total cash outlay of the first two years. The Trust was looking for ways to redirect existing training, audit and research effort to create dedicated improvement time.
actions.sectorNotes: In Moroccan automotive, 90.07% of respondents ranked senior management prioritising time and resources for improvement as the top success factor; healthcare/services cases show the main cost is staff time rather than cash, which matters for SMEs with limited budgets.
actions.pitfalls: Limited resources is one of the most cited Lean Six Sigma failure factors (Albliwi et al., 2014); funding Lean only through external consultants so kaizen stops when they leave.

actions.actionEn: Take an active part in Lean initiatives, for example by sponsoring Kaizen events.
actions.actionFr: Participer activement dans les initiatives Lean, par exemple, en sponsorisant des événements Kaizen.
steps: Each senior manager sponsors at least one kaizen event per quarter: picks the process, sets stretch goals, signs the event charter
Leaders join part of the 3-5 day event (kick-off, gemba, report-out) and remove barriers in real time
Introduce leader standard work with protected gemba time (e.g. daily walks following the value stream)
Attend the 30/60/90-day follow-up to check that gains are sustained
actions.durationBasis: Kaizen events last 3-5 days (Farris/Van Aken research); a first quarterly cycle of sponsored events plus 30-90 day follow-up gives the range (practice)
actions.proof: Kaizen event charters signed by named executive sponsors, attendance records at report-outs, leader standard work sheets and gemba walk logs.
kpis: Leader participation = kaizen events with executive sponsor present at report-out / total events x 100 (%)
Gemba time = hours per leader per week spent at the workplace (h/week)
Sustainment rate = events whose results hold at 90 days / events completed x 100 (%)
actions.example: Wiremold (from late 1991): CEO Art Byrne wrote the training manual, personally led the first year of Lean training (about 150 people) and was a frequent kaizen team member; in just under three years throughput time fell from 4-6 weeks to 2 days or less, inventory fell 80%, some changeovers fell from up to 10 hours to under 10 minutes, sales doubled and profits tripled.
actions.sectorNotes: Manufacturing: sponsorship centres on shop-floor kaizen and changeover/flow; healthcare/services: executives co-lead rapid improvement workshops (Virginia Mason required executives to be certified to lead them).
actions.pitfalls: Leaders who 'send a memo and let somebody else do it' signal that Lean is not real (Byrne); event results often degrade within 6-12 months without management follow-up (Farris/Van Aken).

actions.actionEn: Communicate openly about the progress of Lean initiatives, including successes and lessons learned.
actions.actionFr: Communiquer ouvertement sur l'avancement des initiatives Lean, y compris les succès et les leçons apprises.
steps: Set up visual management boards per area showing Lean KPIs, actions and kaizen results
Run short tiered daily huddles (under 15 min team level, under 30 min upper level) with a standard agenda
Hold monthly Lean report-outs where teams present successes and lessons from failed or stalled kaizens
Keep a visible action register (issue, owner, next step, resolution) and close the loop with staff
actions.durationBasis: Cleveland Clinic rolled out tiered huddles across the organisation in about six months; smaller sites start in 8 weeks (practice)
actions.proof: Active visual boards updated at least weekly, huddle attendance records, monthly report-out minutes including lessons learned, and an action register with closed items.
kpis: Huddle adherence = huddles held / huddles scheduled x 100 (%)
Action closure rate = actions closed on time / actions raised x 100 (%)
Lessons-learned shared = kaizen report-outs published per month (count)
actions.example: Cleveland Clinic introduced tiered daily huddles with a standard agenda and a spreadsheet action register (including who is responsible for fixing each issue), starting at Tier 2 in one area and rolling out in about six months before adding every hospital, across an organisation of some 66,000 caregivers. No quantified outcomes reported in the source.
actions.sectorNotes: Manufacturing uses shift-start production boards; hospitals and services use tiered huddles across shifts and sites; SMEs can run one combined tier.
actions.pitfalls: Weak communication is one of the most frequent LSS failure factors (Albliwi et al., 2014); huddles that become upward reporting instead of local problem-solving, or leaders reporting 'no problems'.

actions.actionEn: Take personal responsibility for the results of Lean initiatives and report on them regularly.
actions.actionFr: Prendre personnellement la responsabilité des résultats des initiatives Lean et en rendre compte régulièrement.
steps: Name an executive owner for each Lean objective and each value stream
Put Lean results on the executive board's monthly agenda with a fixed scorecard
Require 'why' explanations and countermeasures when expected results are missed
Include Lean results in managers' annual objectives and performance reviews
actions.durationBasis: practice; two to three monthly review cycles are needed to establish the routine
actions.proof: Executive board minutes with monthly Lean review, owner-per-objective matrix, and managers' objectives containing Lean KPIs.
kpis: Lean target attainment = Lean objectives on target / total Lean objectives x 100 (%)
Review cadence = monthly executive Lean reviews held / 12 (per year)
Countermeasure closure = missed targets with documented countermeasure / missed targets x 100 (%)
actions.example: Royal Bolton Hospital: the Executive Board reviews each month's Lean activity and asks why when expected results are missing. In the trauma service, over nine months, total length of stay fell 33% and relative risk-adjusted mortality for fractured hips fell by a reported 36% (from 173.9 in 2004/05 to 105.5).
actions.sectorNotes: Healthcare and services report results mainly as quality, safety and flow; manufacturing adds cost, inventory and productivity. Laureani and Antony found 'LSS financial accountability' a distinct leadership factor across sectors.
actions.pitfalls: Accountability placed only on the Lean office instead of line managers; Lean efforts regress when the top leader stops pushing (Byrne).

actions.factorNameFr: Changement de culture pour le Lean
actions.actionEn: Run awareness campaigns so that Lean principles are understood and accepted across the company.
actions.actionFr: Promouvoir des campagnes de sensibilisation pour faire comprendre et accepter les principes du Lean au sein de l'entreprise.
steps: Write a one-page 'why Lean, why now' case linked to customer and safety/quality problems, and state explicitly that Lean is not about headcount cuts
Run short introductory sessions for all staff (incl. support functions) led by a senior manager, covering waste, flow, PDCA and respect for people
Use a hands-on Lean simulation or gemba visit so people see waste in their own process
Invite every team to submit one improvement idea and show visibly that ideas are acted on
Run a short pulse survey before and after to measure understanding and acceptance
actions.durationBasis: practice; UZA Antwerp introductory sessions were the first step of a 2.5-year ward roll-out (Planet Lean)
actions.proof: Attendance records showing >=80% of staff completed the awareness session; pulse-survey results showing understanding of Lean purpose; log of improvement ideas submitted per team.
kpis: Awareness coverage (%) = staff who attended Lean awareness session / total headcount x 100
Acceptance score = mean agreement (1-5) with 'I understand why we are adopting Lean and support it' in pulse survey
Idea participation rate (%) = employees submitting >=1 idea / headcount x 100
actions.example: UZA (Antwerp University Hospital) launched UZALean in earnest in 2011 with introductory sessions led by the chief nursing officer or HR director and a CEO video stating the programme was not about cost-cutting; 220 managers (including 50 physicians) were trained, more than 140 improvement projects were set up, and nurses' direct-care time rose on average about 10% across wards.
actions.sectorNotes: In hospitals and services, framing Lean around quality/safety rather than cost is critical for clinical acceptance; in Moroccan automotive plants Lean (5S, kaizen) typically comes first and is supported by the international parent company.
actions.pitfalls: Starting with tools before people understand the purpose produced low engagement and unsustained gains; fatigue from repeated top-down initiatives and fear of job loss undermine acceptance.

actions.factorNameFr: Changement de culture pour le Lean
actions.actionEn: Encourage and develop transformational leadership through dedicated training and role models.
actions.actionFr: Encourager et développer le leadership transformationnel à travers des formations dédiées et des exemples de rôles.
steps: Define the expected Lean leader behaviours (go to gemba, ask rather than tell, coach problem solving, show appreciation)
Train managers in Lean leadership and have each lead one A3/kaizen in their own area
Put senior leaders on improvement teams and set a gemba-walk cadence (e.g. middle managers monthly, executives quarterly)
Introduce leader standard work and review it in management meetings
Collect 360 feedback on whether leaders model the behaviours
actions.durationBasis: practice; leadership behaviour change needs several coaching cycles (UZA ran manager training with one A3 each)
actions.proof: Leader standard work documents and gemba-walk logs; list of A3s led by managers; 360 or survey results on leader role-modelling.
kpis: Gemba-walk compliance (%) = completed scheduled gemba walks / planned x 100
Leaders coaching rate (%) = managers who led or coached >=1 improvement in the period / total managers x 100
Leader role-model score = mean staff rating (1-5) of 'my manager models continuous improvement'
actions.example: At ThedaCare (Lean from 2002), CEO John Toussaint joined improvement workshops, e.g. physically helping rearrange an obstetrics unit, to show personal commitment; LEI reports $27 million savings since 2002 with no layoffs.
actions.sectorNotes: Laureani & Antony found the need for strong, visible leadership is greater in service/people-centred sectors and in smaller companies; a Dutch hospital study linked lean leadership practices to transformational leadership and lean maturity.
actions.pitfalls: Leaders who delegate Lean to specialists instead of modelling it; lukewarm visible support from leaders undermines the message.

actions.factorNameFr: Changement de culture pour le Lean
actions.actionEn: Identify and actively manage resistance to change by offering suitable training and support.
actions.actionFr: Identifier et gérer activement les résistances au changement en proposant des formations et un soutien adaptés.
steps: Map stakeholders by influence and attitude and hold one-to-one conversations to find the source of resistance
Address job-security fear explicitly (e.g. a no-layoff-due-to-Lean commitment and redeployment of freed capacity)
Co-design changes with the affected team and run small pilots rather than imposing solutions
Offer targeted training and coaching to resistant groups and root-cause their practical objections
Track resistance issues in a log and close each with an action
actions.durationBasis: practice
actions.proof: Stakeholder map and resistance log with actions closed; written employment-security statement; before/after attitude survey per area.
kpis: Resistance issues closed (%) = resistance items resolved / items logged x 100
Change-readiness score = mean (1-5) on readiness survey per department
Voluntary turnover in Lean pilot areas (%) = leavers / average headcount x 100
actions.example: Virginia Mason Medical Center: when some staff and physicians left or chose to 'wait and see' during its Toyota Production System adoption (around 2002), CEO Gary Kaplan required senior leaders to earn TPS certification (seven days of classroom training plus study); early workshops cut patient wait time by 69%.
actions.sectorNotes: In healthcare, clinicians judge Lean against medical logic, so joint problem solving between Lean and clinical staff is needed; in manufacturing, the main fear is job loss from productivity gains.
actions.pitfalls: Poor communication and limited employee involvement are the main drivers of resistance (Canning & Found 2015); layoffs after improvements stop people from improving their own jobs (Wiremold).

actions.factorNameFr: Changement de culture pour le Lean
actions.stageFr: Intégration dans les Processus RH Lean
actions.actionEn: Build Lean principles into HR processes and evaluation criteria.
actions.actionFr: Intégrer les principes du Lean dans les processus et les critères d'évaluation des RH.
steps: Add Lean behaviours (kaizen participation, problem solving, developing others, teamwork) to job descriptions and the annual appraisal
Make Lean training and a completed improvement a criterion for promotion to team leader and above
Include Lean/problem-solving aptitude in recruitment interviews
Adopt an employment-security policy so productivity gains are not converted into layoffs
Give HR a seat on the Lean steering team
actions.durationBasis: practice; aligned to one HR appraisal cycle
actions.proof: Revised appraisal form and job descriptions containing Lean criteria; promotion policy referencing Lean training; HR representative on Lean steering committee minutes.
kpis: Appraisal coverage (%) = appraisals including Lean criteria / total appraisals x 100
Training rate (%) = production staff receiving Lean training in the year / total production staff x 100
Promotions meeting Lean criteria (%) = promoted staff with Lean training and >=1 improvement / total promotions x 100
actions.example: Toyota's annual employee evaluation (as documented by C. Roser from notes on viewed evaluation sheets) puts kaizen involvement, problem solving and leadership (including developing subordinates) in its more important first group of criteria, each worth up to 10 points, and only the jointly agreed employee-supervisor evaluation is used for promotion.
actions.sectorNotes: In 76 Spanish ceramic-tile plants, high Lean adopters trained 13.6% of production staff vs 4.3% and had somewhat more permanent contracts, but pay-for-performance was not linked to Lean; seniority-based pay systems can limit HR alignment.
actions.pitfalls: HR left out of the Lean programme so appraisal and pay still reward old behaviours; Lean implemented with tools only, without the 'people value stream' that develops problem solvers.

actions.actionEn: Recognise and reward behaviours and results that are in line with the Lean culture.
actions.actionFr: Reconnaître et récompenser les comportements et les résultats qui sont en ligne avec la culture Lean.
steps: Define which Lean behaviours and results are recognised (ideas implemented, problems solved, standard work kept, helping others)
Set up an idea/kaizen system with fast feedback and small, consistent rewards
Recognise teams publicly at huddles, kaizen boards and site events; have leaders deliver recognition
Run an annual Lean award for best improvements
Review the scheme yearly for fairness and participation
actions.durationBasis: practice
actions.proof: Written recognition policy; idea-system records showing ideas implemented and rewarded; photos/minutes of recognition events.
kpis: Ideas per employee per year = implemented ideas / average headcount
Idea implementation rate (%) = ideas implemented / ideas submitted x 100
Recognition reach (%) = employees recognised at least once in the year / headcount x 100
actions.example: Toyota's Creative Idea Suggestion System (since 1951) combines small cash awards with annual gold/silver/bronze recognition; a secondary source reports about 810,000 ideas in 2023 (14.4 per person) and a historical implementation rate around 70% (figures not verified against Toyota primary sources).
actions.sectorNotes: In service/knowledge-work Lean programmes, a UK case recommended recognising and rewarding staff participation and using an in-house Lean team rather than consultants.
actions.pitfalls: Pay-for-performance alone showed no link to Lean performance in Spanish plants; linking to HR rewards was rated the least-applied CSF by practitioners (mean 3.04 of 5).

actions.actionEn: Adapt strategic communication to support and highlight Lean initiatives.
actions.actionFr: Adapter la communication stratégique pour soutenir et mettre en avant les initiatives Lean.
steps: Translate the Lean 'true north' into 3-5 breakthrough objectives on an X-matrix or hoshin plan
Run catchball: draft objectives shared with managers who modify, add or delete before adoption (half-day group session)
Cascade objectives into each department's A3 / bowling chart so every team sees its link to strategy
Have the CEO and site leaders restate the Lean case in all-hands meetings and on strategy boards
Review hoshin progress monthly and re-run the planning cycle annually (FAIR: Focus, Alignment, Integration, Review)
actions.durationBasis: Catchball group session takes about a half-day (Howell, LEI 2022); full hoshin cycle is annual (Witcher et al.); 8-16 weeks for the first deployment wave is practice.
actions.proof: Signed X-matrix/hoshin plan showing Lean objectives; minutes of catchball sessions; department A3s that trace to strategic objectives; monthly hoshin review records.
kpis: Strategy alignment rate = departments with an A3 linked to a hoshin objective / total departments x 100 (%)
Hoshin objectives on target = objectives green at monthly review / total objectives x 100 (%)
Employee awareness = staff able to state the top Lean objectives in a gemba check / staff asked x 100 (%)
actions.example: Hewlett-Packard and Xerox UK were studied in depth by Witcher and Butterworth (UEA); their hoshin research produced the FAIR model (Focus, Alignment, Integration, Review), later used by Royal Bolton Hospital NHS Foundation Trust to formulate and deploy strategic objectives (programmes judged effective by managers; no quantified result reported).
actions.sectorNotes: Published hoshin research is mostly manufacturing in the UK/USA (Wilson, Cudney & Marley 2024); healthcare use exists (ThedaCare, NHS, X-matrix simulation by Barnabe & Giorgino 2017). SMEs can use a single-page X-matrix rather than multi-level cascades (practice).
actions.pitfalls: Leaders write the full plan themselves and only ask for edits, losing engagement and people development (Howell 2022); strategy panels on boards go out of date quickly (Bateman et al. 2016).

actions.actionEn: Tailor internal communication so that it is consistent with Lean principles and easy to understand.
actions.actionFr: Personnaliser la communication interne pour qu'elle soit cohérente avec les principes Lean et facilement compréhensible.
steps: Co-design a standard team communication board (daily side + KPI side) with team leaders using paper mock-ups
Apply visual design rules: suitable graph types, minimal colour, layout that follows the briefing order
Replace jargon with plain Lean vocabulary (a one-page glossary of waste, flow, standard work)
Hold a 10-15 minute stand-up at the board at the start of each shift
Coach team leaders on the board for the first weeks, then audit use monthly
actions.durationBasis: Assa Abloy design took three meetings and roll-out took four to six months across about 20 cells (Bateman et al. 2016).
actions.proof: Standard board installed in every cell/team, updated daily; board use audit; time to update the board (Assa Abloy: 12-17 min/week per TL).
kpis: Board compliance = boards updated on schedule / total boards x 100 (%)
Stand-up adherence = stand-ups held / scheduled x 100 (%)
Problems raised at board per week (count)
actions.example: Assa Abloy (lock maker, Willenhall UK, about 320 staff): team leaders co-designed visual management boards; after roll-out, all TLs used the daily side and 10 of 14 cells showed problem-solving in morning meetings.
actions.sectorNotes: Manufacturing cells with daily instability struggle to use boards (Bateman et al.); web/e-mail-only channels miss shop-floor staff without computers (iSixSigma). In services/healthcare, huddle boards work at unit level (ECU 2023 nursing project).
actions.pitfalls: TLs lack skills/software to build graphs so the facilitator ends up doing the design; inaccurate or unsuitable measures (e.g. efficiency) on the board reduce trust (Bateman et al. 2016).

actions.actionEn: Build active listening into management processes to encourage continuous improvement.
actions.actionFr: Intégrer l'écoute active dans les processus de gestion pour encourager les améliorations continues.
steps: Add leader standard work: scheduled gemba walks where managers ask open questions and record issues
Put an idea/improvement board in each team and discuss new ideas in short team meetings (1-4 times per month)
Keep decisions local: the team that raises an idea tests it (PDSA) and escalates only when needed
Respond to every idea quickly, including a reasoned 'no', and post the status visibly
Set and track an idea target (e.g. one idea per employee per year)
actions.durationBasis: practice; St. Mary's reached its one-idea-per-employee target within one year.
actions.proof: Gemba walk log with issues and closure dates; idea board/register with status of each idea; count of ideas implemented per employee per year.
kpis: Ideas per employee per year = ideas submitted / headcount
Implementation rate = ideas implemented / ideas submitted x 100 (%)
Response time = median days from submission to first response
actions.example: St. Mary's General Hospital (Ontario): staff propose, test and measure ideas locally; goal of one idea per employee was beaten with more than 1,300 ideas, and the ICU cut average ventilator time from nine to six days.
actions.sectorNotes: In a Swedish hospital, 89% of kaizen suggestions addressed simple, single-unit issues (Mazzocato et al. 2016); manufacturing ideas mostly concern simplifying processes (Toyota). SMEs can run this without software.
actions.pitfalls: Weak follow-through: only 28% of suggestions recorded results and 17% had manager sign-off (Mazzocato et al. 2016); committee bottlenecks and silence after submission kill participation (KaiNexus).

actions.actionEn: Communicate regularly on the progress of Lean initiatives at every level of the company.
actions.actionFr: Communiquer régulièrement sur les progrès des initiatives Lean à tous les niveaux de l'entreprise.
steps: Design tiered huddles (team, department, site) with a standard agenda: safety, quality, delivery, cost, issues
Time-box huddles (under 15 min lower tiers, under 30 min upper tiers)
Keep an action register (issue, owner, next step, resolution) so issues escalate up and answers come back down
Pilot at one tier in one area, add upper tiers at one site, then extend
Share kaizen report-outs and before/after results on boards and in monthly site meetings
actions.durationBasis: Cleveland Clinic rolled out tiered huddles across the system in about six months.
actions.proof: Tier huddle schedule and attendance; action register with closure dates; visible trend charts of Lean KPIs at each tier.
kpis: Huddle adherence = huddles held / scheduled x 100 (%)
Escalated issue closure time (days, median)
Action closure rate = actions closed on time / actions due x 100 (%)
actions.example: Cleveland Clinic developed a system of tiered daily huddles in early 2018 across an organisation of about 66,000 caregivers; the author reports 'significant learnings and rapid results' but no quantified outcome was in the text opened.
actions.sectorNotes: Healthcare uses safety/patient-experience topics; manufacturing boards focus on SQDC per cell (Bateman et al.). SMEs typically need only two tiers (practice).
actions.pitfalls: Huddles drift without a fixed agenda and time limits; managers asking TLs to use boards inconsistently reduces use (Bateman et al. 2016).

actions.actionEn: Design communication training that takes the specifics of Lean into account.
actions.actionFr: Concevoir des formations en communication qui prennent en compte les spécificités du Lean.
steps: Train managers and team leaders in coaching dialogue (Coaching Kata: five questions on target, actual, obstacles, next step)
Train supervisors in TWI Job Relations (get facts, weigh, act, check) for people issues during improvement
Teach how to run a stand-up meeting and a kaizen report-out
Practise on real cases with daily 10-minute coaching cycles at the board
Evaluate with observed coaching sessions, not attendance only
actions.durationBasis: Kata course was four hours, followed by daily 10-minute coaching over about 10 months (Dinis-Carvalho et al. 2016); TWI JR is a 10-hour course (practice).
actions.proof: Training records of leaders in coaching/JR; observed coaching session checklists; Kata/A3 boards kept up to date by teams.
kpis: Leaders trained = leaders certified in coaching/JR / total leaders x 100 (%)
Coaching cycles per week per team (count)
Improvement result of coached teams (e.g. lead-time reduction %)
actions.example: A wooden molding and frame maker (Dinis-Carvalho et al., IEEE IEEM 2016): four-hour Improvement/Coaching Kata course plus near-daily 10-minute coaching; mean lead time fell from 6.2 h to 0.97 h (-84%) and orders rose over 30% with the same staff.
actions.sectorNotes: Works in small plants: WECO (35 staff, Puerto Rico) trained 20 employees in Kata and lean and reported 31% more output and $42,500 less overtime (NIST MEP). TWI JR is used mostly in manufacturing.
actions.pitfalls: Top-down persuasion fails: the team adopted one-piece flow only after its own experiments (Dinis-Carvalho et al. 2016); training without follow-up coaching.

actions.actionEn: Make sure every employee receives basic training in Lean principles.
actions.actionFr: Assurer que tous les employés reçoivent une formation de base sur les principes Lean.
steps: Define a short Lean awareness module (value, waste/muda, flow, pull, 5S, standard work) linked to the site's own processes
Train a pool of internal trainers (supervisors/team leaders) using TWI Job Instruction's 4-step method
Roll out by area in half-day to one-day sessions with a gemba walk or 5S exercise in the participants' own zone
Add the module to onboarding so new hires get it within their first month
Track coverage per department and run a short knowledge check after each session
actions.durationBasis: Module length sourced: Diageo LCS Level 1a awareness = 1 day for operators; Miami-Dade Yellow Belt workshop = 6.5 h. Rollout window to all staff is practice.
actions.proof: Training register showing % of employees who completed the Lean basics module, attendance sheets, knowledge-check results, and onboarding checklist that includes the module.
kpis: Lean basics coverage (%) = employees trained / total employees x 100
Average knowledge-check score (%) after session
Improvement ideas submitted per trained employee per quarter
actions.example: Diageo (from 2012) adopted a global Lean programme built on the Lean Competency System: a one-day awareness course (LCS Level 1a) for operators and a four-day course (Level 1b) for managers across 97 sites; the REF impact case reports no quantified result.
actions.sectorNotes: Manufacturing typically teaches basics on the shop floor (5S, standard work, TWI); services and public bodies (e.g. Miami-Dade, HMRC) use short classroom workshops with service-process examples. SMEs often skip the formal Lean/Six Sigma split and teach both together (Timans et al., Dutch SMEs).
actions.pitfalls: Awareness training with no follow-up application is quickly forgotten and breeds cynicism; training is mistaken for learning when it stays at PowerPoint level (Lean Construction Institute; LCS).

actions.actionEn: Offer advanced training to develop Lean-specific skills.
actions.actionFr: Offrir des formations avancées pour développer des compétences spécifiques au Lean.
steps: Identify target roles (team leaders, area managers, CI engineers) and their required Lean competencies
Run a practitioner-level programme (VSM, flow/pull, SMED, TPM, A3, kaizen event facilitation) in blocks with homework between sessions
Require each participant to run a real Lean project or kaizen event in their area between workshops
Provide coaching from an experienced Lean lead/Kaizen Promotion Office during the project
Close with a project review presentation to management
actions.durationBasis: ISO 18404-aligned Lean Practitioner courses: two four-day workshops with a Lean project and portfolio in between (St Andrews Lean summary). Total elapsed time is practice.
actions.proof: List of people who completed advanced Lean training, completed project A3s/charters with before-after data, coach sign-off, and management review minutes.
kpis: Advanced-trained ratio (%) = Lean practitioners / supervisory+technical staff x 100
Project completion rate (%) = projects closed with verified results / projects launched
Benefit per project (hours saved, lead-time reduction % or currency)
actions.example: HM Courts & Tribunals Service trained 558 people through LCS Level 2a/2b and implemented Lean across all 500 UK courts, reporting over 66,500 staff hours saved per month, sustained.
actions.sectorNotes: Moroccan automotive firms typically start with foundational Lean (5S, kaizen) and later add advanced methods; parent-company support speeds this up (Kazancoglu et al., IJLSS 2025). Healthcare example: Virginia Mason runs an advanced 'Kaizen Fellowship' for leaders.
actions.pitfalls: Projects too complex or too long to finish during the course; line managers do not release time for the project (LCS '11 ways').

actions.actionEn: Set up a Lean certification programme to validate the skills acquired.
actions.actionFr: Mettre en place un programme de certification Lean pour valider les compétences acquises.
steps: Choose a reference framework (Lean Competency System levels, SME/AME/Shingo Lean Bronze-Silver-Gold, or ISO 18404 Lean Practitioner/Leader/Expert)
Define internal certification criteria: training hours, knowledge exam, completed project(s) with verified results, reference/sign-off
Set up an assessment panel (certified Lean lead + manager) and a portfolio template
Certify the first cohort and publish the register of certified staff
Link certification to role descriptions, career progression and recognition
actions.durationBasis: SME/AME/Shingo Lean Bronze: 80 training credits + exam at 75% + accomplishment record; LCS Level 2: application, two case studies, reference; LCS Level 3: nine-month programme.
actions.proof: Written certification standard, register of certified employees by level, assessed portfolios/case studies, exam results and panel decisions.
kpis: Certified Lean staff (%) = certified employees / target population x 100
Average verified benefit per certification project (currency or hours)
Certification pass rate (%) = certified / candidates assessed
actions.example: Lloyds Banking Group (from 2009) ran a Lean Sigma Academy approved to accredit staff under the Lean Competency System, accrediting about 100 people per year, with an average tangible benefit of GBP 100,000 per accreditation project.
actions.sectorNotes: Lean Bronze/Silver/Gold originated in manufacturing (SME/AME/Shingo); LCS is widely used in services and government (Lloyds, HMRC, BBC, KPMG). For SMEs, ISO 18404 courses cost GBP 2,200+ per person, so internal or LCS-accredited schemes are cheaper.
actions.pitfalls: No universal standard, so certificates of very different rigour are hard to compare (Laureani & Antony 2012); certificates chased for CVs rather than results (Graban/Arthur).

actions.actionEn: Update Lean training content regularly so it reflects the latest best practices.
actions.actionFr: Actualiser régulièrement le contenu de la formation Lean pour qu'il reflète les dernières meilleures pratiques.
steps: Assign an owner (KPO/Lean academy) and an annual review date for every Lean module
Collect inputs: course feedback, project results, audit gaps, new practices (Toyota Kata, digital/visual tools, AR-based TWI)
Revise content, cases and exercises using the organisation's own recent projects
Pilot the revised module with one group before full release
Run short refresher sessions for previously trained staff on what changed
actions.durationBasis: practice (Kaizen Institute academy model: design, content, train-the-trainer, pilot, regular delivery with content kept updated).
actions.proof: Version-controlled curriculum with revision dates, change log tied to feedback/project lessons, pilot evaluation, and refresher attendance records.
kpis: Curriculum currency (%) = modules reviewed in last 12 months / total modules x 100
Training satisfaction / relevance score (1-5) per module

actions.example: La-Z-Boy (Dayton, TN and Siloam Springs, AR) saw its 2005 Lean effort plateau and introduced Toyota Kata in 2011 as daily coaching; reported cell efficiency up 10-28% and defect levels improved 20-50% (IndustryWeek, 2015).

actions.actionFr: Mettre en place une formation pratique sur les outils Lean adaptée à chaque rôle (ateliers, pratique terrain / gemba).
steps: Build a role-based training matrix (operators: 5S, standard work; supervisors: TWI-JI, kaizen; engineers: VSM, SMED, A3)

Create a Lean career track: e.g., Lean practitioner -> kaizen leader -> Lean coach/KPO specialist, with skill level required at each step

actions.pitfalls: Earlier information-sharing attempts often fade without structure (Xerox noted this before formalising its CI network); communities that only share metrics, not mistakes and learning, lose value.

actions.actionEn: Establish a clearly defined Six Sigma strategic charter with measurable objectives.

steps: Executive team drafts a Six Sigma charter: purpose, scope, link to strategy and customer CTQs
Set measurable deployment goals (e.g. DPMO or COPQ reduction, savings target, number of certified Belts and projects by date)
Define governance: deployment leader, champions, steering committee, project selection criteria

actions.example: Motorola (Baldrige Award 1988) stated a goal of 'zero defects in everything we do' with a Six Sigma target of no more than 3.4 defects per million, after a 1981 drive for tenfold quality improvement, with further planned leaps in 1989 and 1991; top-level meetings reviewed quality programmes and results were communicated across the company.
actions.sectorNotes: Manufacturing charters use DPMO/yield; services and banks (e.g. Bank of America) frame targets around customer satisfaction and transaction defects. Moroccan aeronautics experts rated management commitment equally important for Six Sigma and Lean (4.67).
actions.pitfalls: Charter without financial or customer linkage, so projects drift to low-value topics; launching Six Sigma without leaders willing to commit resources (Kwak and Anbari advise not starting in that case).

actions.actionEn: Formally recognise Six Sigma certifications and include them in promotion criteria.
actions.actionFr: Reconnaître officiellement les certifications Six Sigma et les intégrer dans les critères d'avancement.
steps: Adopt a certification standard requiring real projects: e.g., ASQ CSSBB (2 projects with signed affidavits, or 1 project plus 3 years experience) or MBB-reviewed internal standard
Require verified before/after results (e.g., >= $100k benefit or >= 50% metric improvement per project) and a champion sign-off
Make belt level an explicit criterion in promotion and grade descriptions
Set recertification (ASQ every 3 years; MoreSteam standard at most 5 years)
Publish a register of certified belts and recognise them formally
actions.durationBasis: Heritage Valley required sustained gains over 6-12 months before Black Belt designation; Antony (2007) projects under 6 months
actions.proof: Written certification standard; certified-belt register with project affidavits; promotion criteria document referencing belts; recertification schedule.
kpis: Certification rate = certified belts / trained belts x 100
Verified savings per certified Black Belt per year (Antony 2007 cites >= $500k as typical expectation)
% of promotions in grades where belt is required that met the requirement
actions.example: Heritage Valley Health System trained 22 Black Belts in its first wave and granted designation only after gains were sustained 6-12 months; 19 of 22 projects (86%) produced substantial gains, with first-year external training cost of $123,000.
actions.sectorNotes: In non-profit/healthcare settings financial thresholds are replaced by percentage improvement in the key metric (MoreSteam standard).
actions.pitfalls: Certification standards vary widely so belts are not comparable (Laureani and Antony 2012); inadequate rewards and recognition are a top reason for LSS project failure (Antony et al. 2022).

steps: Write one integrated Lean Six Sigma vision inside the corporate strategy (not a separate programme)
Hold a quarterly strategy review where LSS objectives and portfolio are reviewed with the leadership team
Use policy deployment to turn 3-5 strategic priorities into one-year goals, department goals and action plans
Do a mid-year reflection and a year-end review to decide which priorities continue
actions.durationBasis: practice; at least two quarterly meetings are needed to show the routine is established
actions.proof: Strategy document containing LSS objectives, agendas and minutes of at least two consecutive quarterly LSS strategy meetings, and a policy deployment matrix.
kpis: Strategy alignment = LSS projects linked to a strategic priority / total LSS projects x 100 (%)
Meeting cadence = quarterly LSS strategy reviews held / planned (%)
actions.example: Danaher Business System: strategic priorities (five to seven) are broken into one-year goals and cascaded to department goals and individual action plans, with gaps, root causes and countermeasures worked out in policy deployment meetings; Danaher reported almost 30% profitable growth per year (as reported, not attributed solely to DBS).
actions.sectorNotes: Moroccan automotive firms usually start with Lean and add Six Sigma later (also 71% of Moroccan aeronautics experts started with Lean), so an integrated vision should sequence the two.
actions.pitfalls: LSS run as a parallel programme disconnected from strategy; vision not sustained through early difficulties, as transformation takes years (Laureani and Antony).

actions.actionFr: Les dirigeants doivent participer à des projets pilotes d'amélioration et partager leurs expériences.
steps: Select 2-3 pilot projects linked to strategy (mix of a kaizen event and a DMAIC project)
Each executive joins or sponsors a pilot and completes basic LSS training first
Leaders attend the pilot report-outs and present their own learning to peers and staff
Use pilot results to decide the scale-up plan
actions.durationBasis: Pilot DMAIC projects run 3-6 months (Kwak and Anbari); Virginia Mason executive certification took about eight months
actions.proof: Pilot charters naming executive participants, report-out records where leaders presented, and leader training/certification records.
kpis: Leader pilot participation = executives active in at least one pilot / total executives x 100 (%)
Pilot success = pilots meeting charter target / pilots completed x 100 (%)
actions.example: Virginia Mason Medical Center sent its physician and administrative executive leadership to Japan for two weeks in June 2002 to study TPS, and all top leaders (executives and directors) must maintain certification to run improvement workshops; reported results include 51% more gastroenterology capacity and RN patient contact time rising from 32% to nearly 90%.

actions.pitfalls: Insufficient top management involvement is the leading failure factor in the literature (Albliwi et al., 2014); some staff and physicians left or waited it out at Virginia Mason, showing resistance when leaders push.

actions.actionFr: Mettre en place un système de responsabilité pour les résultats des initiatives Lean et Six Sigma avec des indicateurs de performance clés.
steps: Define a balanced LSS scorecard (quality, safety, delivery, cost, people, financial savings) with targets per leader
Write accountability into leaders' objectives and performance reviews
Review the scorecard monthly/quarterly; require countermeasures on misses
Validate results with finance and audit them yearly
actions.durationBasis: practice; needs objective-setting calendar plus two review cycles
actions.proof: LSS scorecard with targets and owners, leaders' objectives with LSS KPIs, review minutes showing countermeasures, finance-validated results.
kpis: Scorecard attainment = LSS KPIs on target / total LSS KPIs x 100 (%)
Productivity improvement = (output per labour hour this year / last year - 1) x 100 (%)

actions.example: ThedaCare's business performance system set a goal of 10% annual productivity improvement with leader standard work (protected daily gemba coaching time); departments achieved 1% to 11% productivity improvements in 2008-2009, and the target was not met in all areas, while rapid improvement events saved tens of millions of dollars, as reported.
actions.sectorNotes: Healthcare balances quality, safety, access and cost rather than a single financial KPI; manufacturing scorecards weigh cost and delivery more heavily (Shingo Model warns lagging KPIs only partly measure behaviour).
actions.pitfalls: Single numeric targets that drive box-checking instead of balanced improvement; tying leaders to cost-cutting only, which keeps LSS from becoming embedded.

actions.actionEn: Create awareness programmes on the importance of cultural change.
actions.actionFr: Créer des programmes de sensibilisation à l'importance du changement culturel.
steps: Run a baseline culture survey (e.g. Shingo Insight or own CI survey) to see where the company stands
Link continuous improvement to a few 'True North' goals cascaded to every team
Hold awareness programmes for all levels explaining why CI matters and how Lean and Six Sigma fit together
Start daily/weekly improvement huddles so CI becomes part of normal work
Repeat the survey after 6-12 months
actions.durationBasis: practice; Berkshire Healthcare's journey from 2017 reached top staff-survey rankings by 2022
actions.proof: Baseline and follow-up culture survey reports; cascaded True North goals; huddle board records in each team.
kpis: CI understanding score = mean (1-5) on 'I understand why continuous improvement matters here'
Team huddle coverage (%) = teams running regular improvement huddles / total teams x 100
Staff involvement score = % agreeing 'I am involved in deciding changes that affect my work'
actions.example: Berkshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust (about 5,000 staff) adopted a Lean/Shingo-based QI approach from 2017 with strategy deployment, huddles and A3; by 2022 it ranked 1st of 190 NHS trusts for staff involvement in deciding changes and 3rd for ability to make improvements happen.
actions.sectorNotes: CSFs are similar across Lean, Six Sigma and earlier change methods; culture and management support matter most regardless of sector (Näslund 2013).
actions.pitfalls: Treating awareness as a one-off launch event; focusing on tools rather than principles (Shingo: tools answer 'how', not 'why').

actions.pitfalls: Linking LSS to HR is the least-applied CSF in practice (Laureani & Antony 2012); HR policies changed on paper but not used in promotion decisions.

actions.sectorNotes: Large multinationals can run multi-level competitions; SMEs and services can use team huddles, newsletters and town-hall recognition at low cost.

Respond within 48 hours and close the loop, including on 'no'
Run regular feedback sessions (team meetings, skip-level sessions) with leaders present

actions.example: Toyota's Creative Idea Suggestion System (since 1951): 789 ideas in the first year; 168,000 in fiscal 1972 from about 43,000 employees; adoption rate rose from 29% (1956) to 76% (1972), supported by monthly themes and an 800-member screening board.

actions.pitfalls: Boxes fail through silence after submission and committee bottlenecks; anonymity blocks follow-up (KaiNexus).

steps: Create one integrated Lean Six Sigma induction module (waste + variation + DMAIC/PDCA) for all new employees
Schedule it within the first weeks of onboarding, delivered by internal trainers

actions.example: San Diego County Health and Human Services Agency reports training its entire staff of 5,936 employees in Lean Six Sigma (White and Yellow Belt open to all), with 62 projects completed; no figures given beyond that (NACo award entry).

actions.pitfalls: Basic training given without allocated time or resources to apply it, which Moroccan practitioners rate as the most critical factor (IEOM 2025).

actions.actionEn: Offer a certification path for employees committed to Lean and Six Sigma.
actions.actionFr: Offrir un parcours de certification pour les employés engagés dans le Lean et le Six Sigma.

Set entry criteria (manager sponsorship), exam pass mark, project and benefit-validation rules
Choose internal certification or an external body (ASQ, IASSC, LCS, ISO 18404, NF X 06-091)

actions.durationBasis: Clients typically aim for internal Green Belt certification within a year and Black Belt within 18 months, often closer to two years (iSixSigma deployment).
actions.proof: Published certification path, number of employees certified per level, project validation files, HR policy linking certification to roles or promotion.
kpis: Certified employees per level (count, % of workforce)

actions.example: GE's legal function required all its lawyers worldwide to reach Green Belt (two to three weeks of training and at least two Green Belt projects) and reported USD 320M of Six Sigma productivity gains in 1999 against a USD 150M goal.
actions.sectorNotes: Service and public organisations often use project-based schemes (ISSSP, LCS) or tiered internal belts (Miami-Dade Yellow/Orange/Blue/Green/Black). French firms can use RS-registered certifications aligned to NF X 06-091 (CESI).
actions.pitfalls: Belts pursued for CV value rather than results (Graban/Arthur); inconsistent certification standards across providers (Laureani & Antony 2012).

actions.actionEn: Offer technical training to develop the skills needed.
actions.actionFr: Proposer des formations techniques pour développer les compétences nécessaires.
steps: Identify project leaders needed vs. available (target ratio of Green Belts and Black Belts to headcount)
Deliver Green Belt (about 40 hours / 1 week) and Black Belt training, each tied to a live project
Train Champions/sponsors (3-5 days) to select and support projects
Run a first wave of pilot projects and review results before scaling
actions.durationBasis: Heritage Valley: first Black Belt wave began about 8 months after decision; admissions project took 7 months; Ford GB 1 week and BB ~16 weeks
actions.proof: Count of trained project leaders by belt; closed pilot projects with measured results; Champion training records.
kpis: Trained project leaders per 100 employees
% of pilot projects delivering target gains (Heritage Valley: 86%)
Verified benefit per project (currency or % metric improvement)
actions.example: ChristianaCare (with Juran Institute) required every Yellow, Green and Black Belt candidate to complete a quality-improvement project in their own area; projects from the first two Green Belt classes produced more than $3 million in savings and/or revenue.
actions.sectorNotes: Healthcare deployments add physician mentors and choose Black Belts for respect across the organisation (Hurley Medical Center); SMEs may train fewer Green Belts and rely on external Black Belt support.
actions.pitfalls: Projects with known answers or no bottom-line value; part-time project leaders often miss the 6-month target (Heritage Valley).

actions.actionEn: Set up a mentoring system to share expertise.
actions.actionFr: Mettre en place un système de mentorat pour le partage de l'expertise.
steps: Set up a mentoring chain: leaders -> Champions -> MBB -> Black Belts -> Green Belts -> team members
Assign named mentors with a fixed cadence (weekly) and a coaching (question-based) style
Require certified experts to teach course modules or mentor as part of their role (e.g., Hurley: certified belts teach sections of DMAIC/Lean courses)
Count mentoring hours in objectives (SME Lean credit scheme counts mentoring hours)
Evaluate mentoring via mentee project results
actions.durationBasis: practice
actions.proof: Mentor-mentee pairing list; mentoring logs; expert objectives including teaching/mentoring; mentee project outcomes.
kpis: % of active belts/practitioners with an assigned mentor
Mentoring hours per expert per month
Mentee project closure rate (%)
actions.example: Hurley Medical Center deployed Six Sigma and Lean with support from North Shore-LIJ, following guidance that past participants be encouraged to complete at least two projects to certify and to teach small sections of DMAIC or Lean courses; no measured results reported.
actions.sectorNotes: Manufacturing/automotive: Toyota Kata coaching at the gemba; services/hospitals: clinical mentors paired with Black Belts; SMEs: external sensei or MEP-type coaches.
actions.pitfalls: Mentors who direct rather than ask; mentoring too infrequent to sustain projects.

actions.actionEn: Offer individual development programmes.
actions.actionFr: Offrir des programmes de développement individualisé.
steps: Run individual competency assessments against an LSS competency framework (EQF-level mapped)
Write individual development plans combining Lean and Six Sigma skills, technical and leadership
Offer differentiated programmes: leader programme (e.g., 8-month Lean for Leaders), belt tracks, advanced fellowships
Use stretch projects and rotations as development vehicles
Review plans in yearly appraisal
actions.durationBasis: SaTH Lean for Leaders ran 8 months per cohort, planned annually
actions.proof: Individual development plans; programme cohort lists; competency re-assessment showing progress.
kpis: % of employees in target population with individual development plan
Programme completion rate (%)
Competency level progression per person per year
actions.example: Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust ran an 8-month Lean for Leaders programme (first cohort ~38-40 ward/department leaders, 55 more planned) where each leader applied the method to a mini value stream with their team; outcome data not yet reported.
actions.sectorNotes: Salentijn et al. (2026) recommend organisations use competency frameworks for role profiles and development paths; evidence base mainly Dutch.
actions.pitfalls: Generic programmes not tied to individual gaps; development without application in own area.

actions.actionEn: Value employees' skills and certifications in performance reviews.
actions.actionFr: Valoriser les compétences et certifications des employés dans les évaluations de performance.
steps: Add LSS certification level and verified improvement results as items in the performance review form
Weight improvement results in variable pay for managers
Link certification to promotion and grade criteria
Recognise certified people and successful projects publicly
Audit yearly that reviews actually use the criteria
actions.durationBasis: practice (one appraisal cycle to change forms and apply them)
actions.proof: Performance review template with LSS items; sample of completed reviews; bonus/promotion policy references.
kpis: % of performance reviews with an LSS skills/certification item completed
% of variable pay linked to improvement goals (management)
Retention rate of certified practitioners (%)
actions.example: GE linked 40% of top management bonus to Six Sigma goals and made Green Belt the minimum for promotion.
actions.sectorNotes: An iSixSigma survey of over 1,300 professionals found leadership development programmes with Six Sigma were six times more likely to be rated highly successful; SMEs may use simpler non-financial recognition.
actions.pitfalls: Inadequate rewards and recognition (Antony et al. 2022); certificates that are not comparable because standards vary (Laureani and Antony 2012).
